kanzAlMahalliRecord.statement: The record scales the original or awl-adjusted case when one or more class shares do not divide exactly over their person counts.

khulasaRecord.locator: references/source-notes/khulasa/khulasa-full.pdf; printed pages 284–288; case correction for one or multiple broken classes.
khulasaRecord.statement: The tashih section gives exact single-class and multi-class correction using divisibility, compatibility, coprimality, and the relations among correction factors.

supportingSourceStatus: No project-local Fath al-Mu‘in locator was available, so none is asserted.
ruleSummary: Correct a case entirely with integer arithmetic so every class's sahm divides exactly among its members.
conditions: The original or awl-adjusted integer case has already been derived.
At least one collective class has integer sahm that do not divide evenly by its person count.
For each broken class, derive its exact correction factor from the class count and class sahm.
exclusions: No correction is applied when every class already divides exactly.
Tashih does not decide heir eligibility, fixed shares, blocking, residuary priority, awl, or radd.
Floating point, decimal approximations, and rounded fractions are not valid sources of the correction factor.
blockingAndPriorityInteractions: Run only after fixed-share, residuary, and awl decisions have produced integer class sahm.
For one broken class, use the whole count under coprimality or the compatible quotient under compatibility.
For multiple broken classes, combine their exact factors using equality, containment, compatibility, or coprimality before scaling every sahm.

sourceAgreement.detail: Both sources describe the same exact integer correction behavior; Khulasa supplies explicit one-class and multi-class examples.

atomicCandidateAssessment.rationale: Single-class and multi-class correction have different factor-combination steps and should be tested independently.

admissionBlockers: Exact examples must become source-derived fixtures before calculation-readiness admission.
